published_prior_art.cite: vonKugelgenEtAl2023UnknownInterventions: its bivariate witness condition is assumed, not proved open dense over arbitrary-DAG sign strata.
vonKugelgenEtAl2023UnknownInterventions: one intervention per node is conjectured for n>2, while its arbitrary-dimensional theorem uses paired interventions.
GrettonEtAl2012KernelTwoSample: observed-input MMD concentration supplies the base layer; the learned-ratio graph application is a routine conditional extension.

Xie2023UniformConditionalCDF and MammenRotheSchienle2012GeneratedCovariates separately cover observed conditional-CDF arguments and generated covariates, not generated indicator thresholds plus generated conditioning coordinates.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 2 / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: Add Jiang and Aragam, Learning nonparametric latent causal graphs with unknown interventions (arXiv:2306.02899v2): it is a close one-unknown-intervention nonparametric latent-graph result under measurement-model graphical assumptions, orthogonal rather than subsuming, but currently omitted.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 1
soundness_flags.one_line: The uniform sup-norm rate has no specified common interior compact domain, first-stage ratio-rate class, or quantitative regularity bound on the arbitrary C2 mixing map, so a uniform attainable r_N is not yet a defined statistical target.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 3
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The learned-ratio MMD guarantee assumes, rather than derives, the simultaneous evaluation-law L1 ratio-error event with radius a_N.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Familywise-valid ancestral-edge recovery conditional on the stated first-stage ratio-error event; no data-driven ratio radius is claimed.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 5–6, Theorems 3.2 and 3.4; p. 9, Conclusions and Discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.2 is bivariate and requires the ratio-law witness in equation (3.2); Theorem 3.4 uses a pair of perfect interventions per node; the discussion explicitly conjectures extension of Theorem 3.2 to n>2 and identifies target-misalignment combinatorics.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 3, Definition 3.2; pp. 4–5, Theorem 4.2; pp. 29–30, Appendix E
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 4.2 identifies CauCA with one intervention per node in a fixed known-graph/known-target model class; the paper distinguishes fully unknown targets and states strong nonidentifiability limits there.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 23–24, Assumption D.1 and Corollary D.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Corollary D.1 obtains element-wise identification from one imperfect intervention per node under a supplied topological order of targets; the paper calls recovery of that order an orthogonal subproblem.

Jiang and Aragam give constructive nonparametric latent-graph recovery from at most one unknown intervention per hidden variable in measurement models, under graphical conditions including complete targets and restrictions addressing imaginary subsets and isolated edges.
The paper establishes MMD two-sample testing and concentration for observed samples, not fitted likelihood-ratio values reused across graph edges.

source_verification_receipts.version: corresponding preprint for Statistics and Probability Letters 201 (2023), journal primary not inspected
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Xie derives uniform bias, rate, and asymptotic-linear results for a local-linear conditional-distribution estimator uniformly in observed response and covariate arguments.

source_verification_receipts.version: corresponding preprint for Annals of Statistics 40(2) (2012)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops stochastic expansions, consistency rates, and asymptotic distributions for nonparametric regression with generated covariates.

The finite-sample CRL result is for general latent causal models with soft interventions and a linear latent-to-observed transformation, so it does not subsume nonlinear shared-diffeomorphic learned-ratio recovery.

The paper establishes open-dense typical faithfulness for Bayesian-network classes, including conditional exponential-family settings, but does not state a surgical likelihood-ratio separation theorem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Jiang–Aragam as an explicit close comparator and state the precise incomparability: their measurement-model graphical assumptions versus this proposal’s invertible shared mixing, smooth mechanisms, and ratio-order certificate.

Make the generated-rank OEQ uniform over a named common compact K and a bounded class for f or for observed ratio smoothness, then state a first-stage ratio rate that the requested expansion conditions on or derives.

Promote the one-intervention decoder’s resource reduction into a sharper comparison table spelling out exactly which assumptions replace the paired-intervention requirement and provide a finite-sample ratio-learner route for at least one bounded observed-ratio subclass.

recommended_next_step: Redraft the survey and make the generated-rank rate question statistically well-posed, then continue to Stage 0 on the population genericity and decoder spine.
